facts: The Order of the Court was as follows: Leave granted in SLPs (Crl.) Nos. 1469-70 of 1990.

These are connected matters. Criminal Appeal No. 642 of 1990 is filed under Section 2 of the Supreme Court (Enlargement of Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction) Act, 1970, while the other appeals are before us pursuant to the leave granted as mentioned above.
These appeals arise out of an occurrence which took place on 30-9-1984 at about 6.45 p.m. on Mukram-Kodakunnam Road near Kottekad.
Bhavadas, the deceased in the case, was travelling in a bus. He got down at the bus-stop, Kottekad.
Meanwhile, the dead body was sent for post-mortem and the doctor who conducted the post-mortem found 11 injuries which could have been caused by a sharp-edged weapon.
The case mainly rested on the evidence of the sole eyewitness, PW 4.
The trial court accepting the evidence of PW 4 convicted Accused 1-11 under Sections 143, 148, 341 and 302 IPC read with Section 149 IPC.
It, however, sentenced Accused 1-4 to imprisonment for life and the others to 7 years' RI except Accused 9-11 who were sentenced to 5 years' RI on the ground that they were not armed with weapons.
The convicted accused preferred appeals to the High Court. The State also preferred an appeal against the order of acquittal of the murder charge.
From the above-stated facts, it can be seen that the case entirely rested on the evidence of PW 4.
It is held in a number of cases by this Court that when the case rests on the testimony of the sole eyewitness, then his evidence must be wholly reliable.

When a sole witness claims to have witnessed the occurrence, but does not come forward as a witness at any time either during the inquest held or earlier, then his evidence is to be scrutinised with great care and caution.
Further, we find that PW 4 is not altogether a disinterested witness. He stood as a surety for one of his partymen in which the appellants appeared as accused.

With this background, if we examine the evidence of PW 4, we find that the explanation given by him for not coming forward as a witness for such a long time does not appear to be plausible and acceptable.

PW 4 deposed that since there were a number of cases between the two parties and he apprehended danger to his own life, he went to his wife's house and only when the police came there, he came forward and gave statement.
It may be mentioned here that PW 4 happened to travel in the bus on that fateful day because he wanted to pay a visit to his mother in that place where the deceased also was living.
Consequently, the appeals are allowed and the convictions and sentences awarded against all the appellants are set aside.
The appellants who are in jail shall be set at liberty if not required in any other case.

court_reasoning: When the case rests on the testimony of the sole eyewitness, then his evidence must be wholly reliable.
It is held in a number of cases by this Court that when the case rests on the testimony of the sole eyewitness, then his evidence must be wholly reliable.
The High Court has not accepted his evidence in respect of at least 6 out of the 11 accused named by him as assailants.
Having perused the evidence as well as the other surrounding circumstances, we find it highly unsafe to rely on the sole testimony of PW 4 to base the convictions
We have also examined the cross-examination and find that some of the important omissions elicited and the discrepancies are very material.
